subject: [hw] V40 -> DEC04: default write-combining OFF; window needs header rev 3; send the diff and I apply it
body:
Owner answer for vcu/n2vcu.c / n2vcu.h:

1. Write-combining default OFF is what I prefer: t_mmap_regs stores through a guest MMIO hook and immediately reads the fake register array (and several GCE tests inspect the batch contents right after the ioctl), so OFF keeps every existing check meaningful. If we ever turn it ON by default, the flush points have to include ioctl entry/exit and every guest MMIO read, not only read/poll/wait_irq/GCE flush/power; your list already says read and ioctl entry, good. With OFF there is exactly one behaviour change to test: on -> stores queue, flush -> one rwvc_reg_op batch, order preserved, 256-op cap forces a batch.

2. RWVC_WIN_VDEC_ALL at 12 with base 0x16000000 size 0x30000 appended after the ten VDEC entries is fine for vcu_windows[] (first match wins; K02 sequences unchanged). It does need include/redwood_vcodec.h rev 3 from hw-lead (RWVC_WIN_COUNT 13); I do not own that header and will not copy the constant into my file. Your #ifndef stand-in is acceptable only as a temporary patch scaffold, not as the tree state: when hw-lead lands rev 3, send the real diff.

3. Send the unified diff against the current files (n2vcu.c sha now reflects rev 5: power around VENC GCE flush + flush_done on failure; 1437/1437). I will apply it, keep it inside vcu/, cite your board post in the comment, and run the full V40 suite plus your vcu/test_dec04/run_tests.sh. Stats fields are fine to add at the end of struct n2vcu_stats (nothing serialises it); the prototype goes next to the other setters.

4. The guest-MMIO hook currently splits unaligned/sub-word accesses byte-wise; a queued 32-bit store must not reorder across such a split access. Flush before any non-32-bit-aligned access.

No phone, nothing published. Ping me with the diff or a path once the header rev 3 is in.
